# shinyOAuthDB

shinyOAuthDB helps you build Shiny apps that query a database or data
platform using each app user’s own account. People sign in with the
account they already use for that data source, and your app queries data
on their behalf.

This is useful when you or your organization already manage accounts and
data permissions in a database or data platform. Your Shiny app can
reuse those permissions, so you don’t have to maintain a separate set of
user accounts and data-access rules in the Shiny app. For example, if
your database limits an analyst to sales data for their region, your
Shiny dashboard can query the data as that analyst and automatically use
the same restriction.

The OAuth sign-in and data access work like this:

1.  A user navigates to your Shiny app. Your Shiny app shows a **Sign
    in** button (shinyOAuth can also redirect users to the provider
    automatically). When the user clicks this button, the app uses
    shinyOAuth to start the OAuth sign-in flow. The user is sent to the
    sign-in page of the database or data platform, or to a trusted
    sign-in service (like your organization’s login service).
2.  The user signs in with their existing account and, if asked,
    approves the access your app requests.
3.  They return to your Shiny app and shinyOAuth obtains an **access
    token**, a temporary credential that lets your Shiny app request
    data on their behalf.
4.  Your Shiny app uses shinyOAuthDB to send that token with its data
    requests. The database or data platform checks the token and applies
    that user’s permissions before returning data.

shinyOAuthDB provides R functions to streamline the above steps, with
configurations for various databases and data platforms. It also helps
you open database connections, run queries, and make API calls.
Depending on the data source, you can work with familiar tools such as
DBI and dbplyr, or use a supporting package’s query and API helpers.

Supported databases and data platforms (links open their setup guides):

## Install

``` r

if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("remotes")
}
remotes::install_github("lukakoning/shinyOAuthDB")
```

## Example usage with PostgreSQL

Below is a minimal example of a Shiny app that queries a PostgreSQL
database.

It launches PostgreSQL and Keycloak sign-in in Docker (so install and
launch [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/) if you wish to
run it).

This example uses PostgREST since it does not require a database driver
to be installed, but you could also use DBI with a PostgreSQL driver.
See the [PostgreSQL
guide](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/articles/postgres.html)
for that.

``` r

library(shiny)
library(shinyOAuth)
library(shinyOAuthDB)

# Start a local demo with PostgreSQL and Keycloak sign-in in Docker
demo <- oauth_db_demo("postgrest", action = "services")

# Create an OAuth client for the demo Keycloak server
client <- oauth_client(
  demo$provider,
  client_id = "shiny-db",
  client_secret = "demo-client-secret",
  redirect_uri = "http://localhost:18100",
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "database.read")
)

ui <- oauth_ui(
  fluidPage(
    actionButton("login", "Sign in"),
    actionButton("logout", "Sign out"),
    tableOutput("rows")
  ),
  id = "auth",
  client = client
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  auth <- oauth_module_server("auth", client, auto_redirect = FALSE)
  observeEvent(input$login, auth$request_login())
  observeEvent(input$logout, auth$logout())

  postgres <- oauth_db_postgrest_api(
    auth$connection,
    url = demo$url
  )
  output$rows <- renderTable({
    postgres$select("visible_rows", order = "row_id.asc")
  })
}

runApp(
  shinyApp(
    ui, server, 
    uiPattern = ".*", 
    onStart = function() { onStop(demo$stop) }
  ),
  port = 18100,
  launch.browser = FALSE
)

# Open the app in your regular browser at http://localhost:18100
# (viewers in RStudio/Positron/etc. cannot perform necessary redirects)
```

Sign in as `alice` / `alice` or `bob` / `bob` (username / password). The
first build takes a few minutes; your browser may ask you to accept the
local sign-in certificate. Stopping the app removes its Docker services.

For your own PostgreSQL server, follow the
[PostgreSQL](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/articles/postgres.html)
or
[PostgREST](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/articles/postgrest.html)
guides. For other databases and data platforms, refer to the links
above.

## Learn more

[Getting
started](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/articles/getting-started.html)
walks through this app, explains OAuth settings, and covers connections,
sessions and saved results. Use the source guides above for the setup
and query methods specific to your database or data platform.

### More demos

The package includes various demo apps.

[`oauth_db_demo()`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_demo.md)
runs local Docker demos for PostgreSQL and other self-hosted databases.
[`oauth_db_cloud_demo()`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_cloud_demo.md)
guides demos for several cloud platforms, during which you will be
walked through first setup with your existing platform workspace and
account.

See [Getting
started](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/articles/getting-started.html#more-ways-to-try-an-app),
[`?oauth_db_demo`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_demo.md)
and
[`?oauth_db_cloud_demo`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_cloud_demo.md)
for the demo options.

# Package index

## Overview and demos

- [`shinyOAuthDB`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/shinyOAuthDB-package.md)
  [`shinyOAuthDB-package`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/shinyOAuthDB-package.md)
  : Query data with a Shiny user's own account
- [`oauth_db_demo()`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_demo.md)
  : Run a local database OAuth demo
- [`oauth_db_cloud_demo()`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_cloud_demo.md)
  : Set up an editable Shiny demo for a cloud workspace

## Shared helpers

Microsoft sign-in and custom connection or token helpers for use across
data sources.

- [`oauth_db_microsoft_client()`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_microsoft_client.md)
  : Set up Microsoft sign-in for database access
- [`oauth_db_connect()`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_connect.md)
  : Connect another database package to a user's sign-in
- [`oauth_db_token()`](https://lukakoning.github.io/shinyOAuthDB/reference/oauth_db_token.md)
  : Get a user's access token for another R package
